failure_summary.description: Explicit travel dates supplied in response to a date question were treated as missing despite enough itinerary context to search.
A new party-size or proposed-location criterion was ignored even though compatible cached results were available.
Search or filter results were not saved to the cache.
A time follow-up used invalid time formatting and searched anew instead of filtering compatible cached flights.
The generated code imported a nonexistent tools module.

patch.reasoning: Clarify how to interpret dates in answers to travel-date questions and how to encode clock-time constraints, addressing the repeated incomplete-date errors and the invalid time-range call. Cache persistence, cached-result updates, and the no-import contract are already stated clearly, including in the protected section, so repeating them would not patch a skill gap.

edits.target: Associate dates with explicitly stated itinerary legs in the order and context given, and do not ask again for dates already supplied.
edits.content: When the user supplies a preferred or ideal travel date in response to a question about travel dates, treat it as a usable itinerary date, not as missing. For an already-requested trip, use the stated travel date as the flight departure date and, when lodging is requested, as check-in if the user has supplied a stay duration; use an explicitly stated return date for the return-leg departure and hotel checkout. Calculate checkout from a known duration in nights with `adjust_date`. Do not apply this mapping to an event date or infer unrequested domains or legs.

edits.target: For range-shaped fields, encode an explicitly exact value as both endpoints (for example, `[n, n]`); encode a minimum rating or a request for at least or better as `[n, schema_max]`.
edits.content: For time-range fields, use the schema's accepted clock notation (for example, `08:23 PM`), not 24-hour values with seconds unless the schema requires them. Encode an exact time as `[time, time]`; encode “by” or “until” a time as `[12:00 AM, time]`, and “at or after” a time as `[time, 11:59 PM]`.
